status: direct path works on a real receiver; HEVC does not pass the clip gates here and stays unqualified

stand.receiver: Chrome 157 on Native, real Intel Iris Xe GL on an owned virtual KWin, iHD VA-API, no VM and no VirGL
stand.server: exp213 worker and bridge on the Native lab VM, repository viewer
stand.gpu_guard: Kernel GPU fault count before and after each run stayed 0; lab VM unchanged

route_limit: The media goes from Native through the controller and back, so feedback delay is about 270 ms against about 125 ms on the Firefox reference. Absolute figures and the narrow-path gates are not comparable with other lanes; compare only within this table.

hevc_qsv_floor_26_32.note: Raising QSM_DIRECT_CROPPED_QMIN from 20 to 26 and 32 left the bytes unchanged: hevc_qsv did not act on the floor in this setup.

receiver: Every HEVC run: codec video/H265, direct decode active, no failure, 0-1 frames dropped, about 1 ms decode per frame.
findings: The viewer now starts direct decode from an HEVC SPS. Before this it fell back to the browser path on any HEVC stream.
HEVC encoded fewer frames at the sender than H264 on both Intel encoders, about 40 against 46 per second, so the loss starts before the network. Why was not established.
HEVC used about three times the bytes on an open path. The H264 floor does not carry over.
not_measured: hevc_nvenc and AMD HEVC against this receiver
A route without the controller hop
recommendation: Keep H264 as the default. Offer HEVC only as an unqualified option until the sender rate and frame cadence are solved.
